Confidence interval for Cramer's V

Source: R/bootstrap_ci.R
sframe_cramers_v_ci.Rd

The noncentrality interval for the association strength in a contingency table, as effectsize::cramers_v(adjust = FALSE, alternative = "two.sided") computes it: the 2-sided interval for the noncentrality of the chi-square statistic, each bound turned into V as \(\sqrt{\lambda / (n (k - 1))}\), where k is the smaller of the number of rows and columns. For a 2 by 2 table V equals phi. The interval reaches 0 when the test is far from significant. Until 0.4.3 this was a percentile bootstrap, whose resampled V is 0 or above, so an exactly independent table had the interval [0.05, 0.50] beside V = 0 (FR-24).

Usage

sframe_cramers_v_ci(tab, R = 2000, conf.level = 0.95, seed = NULL)

Arguments

tab

A contingency table (from table()) or a matrix of counts.

R

Kept so existing calls still run. Unused since 0.4.3.

conf.level

Confidence level. Defaults to 0.95.

seed

Kept so existing calls still run. Unused since 0.4.3, as the interval uses no resampling.

Value

A named numeric vector: estimate, lower, upper, with the attributes level and method ("noncentral chi-square"). The bounds are NA when the table holds fewer than 3 observations or has fewer than 2 rows or columns.

See also

sframe_eta_sq_ci(), sframe_bootstrap_ci()

Other Confidence interval functions: sframe_bootstrap_ci(), sframe_cohens_d_ci(), sframe_eta_sq_ci()

Examples

sframe_cramers_v_ci(table(mtcars$am, mtcars$cyl))
#>  estimate     lower     upper 
#> 0.5226355 0.1118233 0.8455313 
#> attr(,"level")
#> [1] 0.95
#> attr(,"method")
#> [1] "noncentral chi-square"
